chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who had three daughters, and he married one of them to a man, but he did not specify to the groom or to the witnesses which daughter he was marrying. The groom had set a dowry for her. When it was time for her to be introduced to the groom, the groom learned that she was the eldest. The groom said to her father, 'I only married the youngest of your daughters.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'If the groom saw all of them and did not specify one of them, then the word of the father is decisive, and it is upon the father, between him and God, to give the groom the daughter whom he intended to marry to him at the time of the marriage contract.' He said, 'And if the groom did not see all of them and did not specify one of them at the time of the marriage contract, then the marriage is invalid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a marriage contract if the father does not specify which daughter is being married?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) in marriage contracts, distinguishing between cases where the groom has visual certainty of the bride's identity versus those where ambiguity remains. It establishes that if the groom saw all three daughters, the father's subsequent designation is binding, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the wali's authority when conditions are met; however, if the groom had not seen them, the contract is void due to lack of specific identification. This ruling underscores the necessity of clear object identification (*ma'qud 'alayh*) for the validity of *nikah* in Shia jurisprudence.
